findings.excerpt: title: Rank-two systems A_2, B_2 and G_2
findings.symptom: The H1 displays A_2, B_2 and G_2 with literal underscores instead of mathematical subscripts. This is a title typography/rendering defect; the corresponding body notation is typeset.
findings.suggested_repair: Use math-aware title rendering or spell the rank-two types in plain text (for example, A2, B2, G2) so the underscores do not appear literally.

findings.excerpt: **Proof technique:** direct: derive the rank-one Verma submodule and quotient from the PBW model, then identify both projective covers for every $n\ge0$ and specialise to $n=0$.
findings.symptom: The uppercase technique banner is intentional, but the embedded $n\ge0$ is rendered as literal dollar and backslash math source rather than typeset mathematics.
findings.suggested_repair: Move the mathematical condition out of the technique banner or convert it to plain text (for example, “for each nonnegative n”), keeping the banner itself in its intended uppercase style.

diagram_candidates.excerpt: The following configurations with six, eight and twelve roots in the plane realize A2, B2 and G2; the item gives the six-unit-vector construction for A2, the eight coordinate/sum vectors for B2, and an explicit twelve-vector model for G2.
diagram_candidates.symptom: The example describes three planar root configurations but the rendered body contains no root-system figure.
diagram_candidates.suggested_repair: Consider a three-panel planar figure: A2 as six equally spaced unit roots with simple roots α=u0 and β=u2; B2 with the eight vectors ±e1, ±e2, ±e1±e2 and simple roots α=e1−e2, β=e2, visually distinguishing short and long roots; G2 with ±α, ±β, ±(α+β), ±(α+2β), ±(α+3β), ±(2α+3β), marking α and β and the positive-root choices. Check the counts (6, 8, 12), reflection symmetry, and Cartan products 1, 2, 3 against lines 43–47.

diagram_candidates.excerpt: The item gives 0→Δ(n)→P(−n−2)→Δ(−n−2)→0 and states head/socle L(−n−2) with middle factor L(n); for n=0 it specializes to 0→Δ(0)→P(−2)→Δ(−2)→0.
diagram_candidates.symptom: The projective structure and the nonsplit filtration are described algebraically, but no Loewy or composition-factor diagram is drawn.
diagram_candidates.suggested_repair: Consider a two-part composition diagram: P(0)=Δ(0)=L(0), and P(−2) with top/head L(−2), middle factor L(0), and bottom/socle L(−2). Annotate the nonsplit submodule Δ(0) and quotient Δ(−2)=L(−2), and state that the picture records composition layers rather than a direct-sum decomposition. The source gives the corresponding general-n structure in lines 70–73.
